source.check: no nomination was received for Dromore; the retiring member was to be declared re-elected: 'No nomination was received for Dromore district, but Mr. W. Liddell (U.) will be declared re-elected' (Northern Whig, 9 May 1936, p. 8; page image read)

note: Triennial election of Down County Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1936 (Belfast News-Letter, 13 April 1936, p. 10). There were no contests. The Northern Whig of 9 May 1936 (p. 8) lists the twenty members who 'will comprise the new County Council', without divisions; each division is taken from the 1933 return or from the 1936 reports of the three changes (Bangor, Garvaghy, Portaferry: Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1936, p. 15; Dromore Leader, 9 May 1936, p. 2) and Comber (J. M. Andrews's election notice, Northern Whig, 8 May 1936). No one was nominated for Dromore, where the retiring member, W. Liddell, was declared re-elected; he resigned and James Ervine was co-opted (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). William Liddell resigned for business reasons; the council accepted the resignation at its first meeting, 18 June 1936, and co-opted James Ervine in his place in August 1936 (Belfast News-Letter, 19 June 1936, p. 13; 7 August 1936, p. 10). The co-option is not an election. The Irish News (8 May 1936, p. 5) had expected a co-option. Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
